tmp:3010: ha-seder she-yesh la-zera'im — the divinely ordained order/arrangement governing seeds and their growth, the natural regularity sustained by faith that lets herbs sprout for healing
tmp:3011: koach ha-refuah — the healing power/efficacy inherent in medicinal herbs, whose potency depends on faith-drawn rains
tmp:3014: asavim ha-gedelim — medicinal herbs as growing plants, the vegetal source of all remedies that sprout only through rains drawn by faith
tmp:3016: the sick person's sweating — the clinical moment when a choleh breaks into sweat and joy is immediately drawn upon him, empirical sign that sweat produces simchah
tmp:3018: simchat Yom Tov — festival joy, 'v'samachta b'chagekha' (Deut 16:14), the rejoicing of a 'good day' produced by holy sweat (extended to any day that is bechinat tov)
tmp:3020: damim zakim — clear/pure blood, the physiological state of unclouded blood that is the bodily substrate of joy
tmp:3021: expulsion of the venom (eres) lodged in the murky blood — the toxin in turbid spleen-blood being discharged outward via sweat
tmp:3022: chalashut — weakness/faintness, the debilitated bodily state caused by blood disorder, opposite of vigor and joy
tmp:3023: the murkiness of blood confined in due measure to the spleen — turbid blood kept in its proper organ-boundary (the techol) rather than spreading
tmp:3024: the blood remaining clear (damim zekhim) — the resulting purified-blood state once murkiness is confined to the spleen, enabling joy
tmp:3025: sweating through a holy matter — the act of exerting oneself to perspiration in a davar shebikdushah, the 'good sweat' that generates joy
tmp:3026: entering the Sea of Wisdom where Malkhut is revealed — R. Yehoshua's vision of the great light in the yam (Bava Batra aggadah), Leviathan = Malkhut disclosed within supernal Chokhmah
tmp:3027: inclusion of the student within the aspect of son — the talmid being incorporated into bechinat ben ('mah'-perception) so that he attains yirah
tmp:3029: Yam ha-Chokhmah — the kabbalistic Sea of Wisdom, supernal Chokhmah as ocean from which Malkhut receives parnasah
tmp:3030: studying and discussing a chiddush of the chakham ha-dor — the act of reviewing the generation's sage's novel Torah teaching, which arouses the Sea of Wisdom
tmp:3031: fear falling upon the one who studies the chiddush — the yirah that descends on the reviewer because Malkhut (source of fear) arrives to draw sustenance
tmp:3032: the fats/oils of the lung in balanced temperament (mezeg ha-shaveh) — equilibrium of the re'ah's shemanim that makes the light of the countenance shine ('to brighten the face from oil')
tmp:3036: chanukat ha-bayit / Chanukah — the dedication of the Temple effected through 'selach na' on Yom Kippur, the festival Chanukah as rectification of the churban
tmp:3037: 'Selach na' — Moshe's plea 'please forgive' (Num 14:19), the Yom Kippur forgiveness-petition whose letters hint at Chanukah
tmp:3038: the drawing down of parnasah via Malkhut — sustenance channeled through the sefirah Malkhut, which gathers everyone's trust and receives food from the supernal 'hands'
tmp:3040: the ability to draw down sustenance through dominion — the husband's/ruler's memshalah ('he shall rule over you') empowering him to channel parnasah to dependents
tmp:3041: et ha-akhilah — the time of eating, the meal as the occasion for receiving the illumination of the will (he'arat ha-ratzon)
tmp:3042: illumination of the aspect of 'mah' — the shining of the unknowable 'what'-perception (wordless longing for God) received at eating by the ish chayil
tmp:3043: so that he not be nullified out of existence and instead have yirah — the protective purpose of interincluding son/student: preventing bittul bimtziut and preserving fear
tmp:3044: meriting to raise up many students (ha'amadat talmidim harbeh) — the pedagogic achievement through which one attains the makifim
tmp:3045: attaining the makifim — meriting to grasp the surrounding/encompassing lights, understanding what was previously beyond one's intellect
tmp:3047: 'all need him' — the universal dependence of great and small alike on the sage who can illuminate every level, hence his many students
tmp:3048: the sage's power to teach everyone — his capacity to learn with all, high dwellers and low, giving each the perception suited to him
tmp:3049: 'he will raise many students' — the certain outcome that the sage with such attainment establishes numerous talmidim (fulfilling Avot 1:1)
tmp:3050: shetok — the divine command 'Be silent! So it arose in thought' (Menachot 29b), silence as fence before the trans-temporal makifim
tmp:3051: not entering makifim that need not/cannot be grasped — the restraint against penetrating surrounding lights above time whose questions time cannot resolve
tmp:3052: revealing the inner intellect (sekhel penimi) — the act of disclosing one's internalized understanding to students, which vacates space for new light
tmp:3053: a new further intellect arising in thought — the fresh makif-sekhel that 'ascends in machshavah' to replace the inner intellect once revealed
tmp:3054: the sage's makifim entering inward — the surrounding lights of the chakham ha-dor becoming internalized when he instills his da'at in students (bechinat length of days, World to Come)
tmp:3057: the surrounding intellect entering within (sekhel makif nikhnas lifnim) — the general dynamic whereby teaching a friend da'at and yirat shamayim internalizes one's makif
tmp:3058: 'his fear of sin precedes his wisdom' (Avot 3:9) — yirat cheto as prerequisite ordering, fear before chokhmah so one's words endure
tmp:3059: 'whoever has fear of Heaven, his words are heeded' (Berakhot 6b) — yirat shamayim in the speaker as the condition making speech effective and lasting
tmp:3060: teaching him Torah and instilling da'at in him — the formative act by which a master makes his student into an 'adam' (before which he was mere human likeness)
tmp:3061: 'one who teaches his friend's son Torah' (Sanhedrin 99b) — the Talmudic case defining the teacher-as-maker, grounding student = son
tmp:3062: 'as if he made him' (ke'ilu asa'o) — the Talmudic dictum crediting the Torah teacher with creating the student's very being/body
